checks.text: V5_PI_USB (Pi 4 downstream USB (4 ports, shared)): avg 0.55 A of 1.2 A (46%), peak 1.05 A of 1.2 A (88%)

webcam sees 4.40 V at its 500 mA descriptor (4.56 V at a typical 250 mA) through its own captive 1.5 m cable; USB floor 4.75 V, most cameras run to ~4.4 V. If it drops out at 1080p, run 720p — its cable cannot be shortened
A 1 m 28 AWG phone cable to the Pi would drop 1.06 V → 3.84 V at the Pi = brownout. The bank cable is a spec: ≤ 0.3 m with ≥ 24 AWG power conductors (any '3 A fast-charge' cable)
Motor phases run 1.5 A through Dupont 2.54 contacts rated 2.0 A — inside rating but the crimp quality is the margin. A contact that heats in the wheels-up test gets re-crimped or soldered.
Tilt servo stall 2.5 A through the PCA9685's 2.54 mm channel header (rated 2.0 A). Momentary, and how every servo board works; keep stalls short with tilt limits in software

DRV8825 nENABLE has an internal pull-down: during the R4's ~1 s reset window (boot, watchdog, sketch upload) D8 floats and all four drivers are ENABLED at full holding current. Add a 10 kΩ pull-up from the shield's EN pin to its 5 V header (consumables). The R4-unpowered case is still the power-up order
No fuse on the pack and no cell alarm (declined). A 2200 mAh 80C pack delivers >70 A into a short; the T-plug is a disconnect, not protection. Listed under Safety as reviewer-recommended.
Pi 5 only: default 600 mA USB cap → set usb_max_current_enable=1, or use the Pi 4 this file assumes.
bank → Pi USB-C cable: 24 AWG × 0.3 m, peak 2.49 A (ampacity 3.5 A, USB-C 3.0 A), round-trip drop 126 mV = 2.5%
Load-test the bank at 2.5 A for 60 s with the meter on the Pi's 5 V pin: below 4.8 V the bank is not a 3 A bank.

If the bank's output is USB-C and the Pi 4 is an early board (pre-2020, rev 1.1), an e-marked C-to-C cable will not power it — use an A-to-C cable or a plain C-to-C. Later Pi 4s and all Pi 5s are fine
Before connecting SDA/SCL: power each I2C module alone and meter SDA to GND — it must read ≤ 3.3 V. A module whose pull-ups go to 5 V goes on 3.3 V power or not on the Pi.

BCM 4/5 have NO on-board I2C pull-ups (BCM 2/3 have 1.8 kΩ). The MLX90640 module must carry its own, or add 4.7 kΩ from SDA and SCL to 3.3 V (consumables). And w1-gpio (1-Wire) defaults to BCM 4 — leave that overlay off

PCA9685 VCC is 3.3 V, so the tilt servo gets 3.3 V PWM. MG996R clones normally accept it; if the servo jitters or ignores commands, that is the level. Do NOT raise VCC to 5 V — the board's I2C pull-ups follow VCC and would put 5 V on the Pi's SDA/SCL. A 74HCT125 buffer fixes it
1000 µF electrolytic across VMOT: stripe = negative, to the GND terminal. Reversed, it vents on the first power-up

ESP32 #2 and #3 are NOT on the rover. Walleye's csi_rx firmware writes CSI to Serial (a wire to the Pi), and the RuView firmware's nodes are receivers of the AP's frames — so the transmitter is the Pi's own 2.4 GHz hotspot on the rover, and the two nodes sit at the doorway and the far wall on any USB power, streaming CSI back over that same WiFi as UDP. Two bistatic links through two walls, zero rover wiring, nothing on the Pi's USB budget.

DRV8825 into the shield socket with its EN pin over the socket's EN label (the trimpot ends up toward the shield's power terminal on genuine Pololu layouts; clones vary — go by the label). Backwards = dead driver on power-up, no warning
The 40 mm fan must be a 5 V fan for the LM2596 rail. A 12 V fan goes on the pack side (Wago +/−, 11.1 V nominal) instead — check the label before it is wired
Servo return: PCA9685 V+ GND terminal → XL4015 OUT− (its own wire). Motor return: shield GND terminal → Wago. Neither ever through a board GND pin or a USB cable.

LM2596 OUT feeds three loads (fan, LD2410C, LD2450): four conductors per polarity, so two MORE 5-way Wagos (four of the pack of ten used) or a soldered splice. Never daisy-chain through a load's connector
DRV8825 1/16 = M2 only → ONE cap on MS3 under each driver, MS1/MS2 open. Four caps, plus the D12 and D13 jumpers on the A header = six jumpers total. Caps go on before the drivers.
Motor coil pairs by multimeter: the two leads that show ~2 Ω are one coil. A coil split across the 2B/2A–1A/1B header halves makes a motor buzz and not turn.

Each radar's GND pin gets TWO wires: one to the LM2596 OUT− (its power return) and the cable's GND to ESP32 #1 (signal reference). With only the cable GND, the radars' 180 mA returns through ESP32 #1 → Pi → R4 USB → shield → Wago: 72 mV of ground shift on every serial link. That is the exact Ceres fault
Power-up: bank → Pi → R4 (USB) FIRST, then the pack at the T-plug. DRV8825 nENABLE floats LOW = enabled; with VMOT alone four motors sit at full holding current with nothing commanding them.
ESP32-S3 #1 firmware must call WiFi.mode(WIFI_OFF): with its radio on, Pi USB peak is 1.20 A of 1.2 A — the port limiter trips and takes the R4's power and serial link with it
Read the sense resistor on one driver: R100 → Vref = 0.75 V for 1.5 A; R200 → 1.50 V. Set all four with the multimeter, motors unplugged, before any motor is connected.
